predecessors.name: Central African Republic
predecessors.text: the north and east of the Central African Republic, from the towns seized on 10 December 2012 to the partition of the end of 2014

successors.name: Central African Republic
successors.text: the five prefectures of the ex-Séléka north and east still held after the government's February 2021 captures, at the disarmament and dissolution of the UPC

ledger.x: 10 December 2012: the Séléka rebels seize their first towns.
End of 2014: the ex-Séléka groups hold the north and east.
14 December 2015: Séléka leaders declare the Republic of Logone.

February 2021: the government retakes Bria (the FPRC's capital), Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture and Nzacko: 'captured a number of strategic towns throughout February 2021, including towns of Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture, Nzacko, Bossembele, Bouar, Beloko and Bossangoa'.
11 July 2025: the UPC and 3R sign disarmament agreements.

wars.name: Central African Republic Civil War
wars.outcome: Séléka seized the capital in March 2013; Djotodia resigned on 10 January 2014; the country was de facto partitioned by the end of 2014; the CPC offensive of 19 December 2020 was repelled at Bangui on 13 January 2021 and the government retook strategic towns…

certainty.note: The land held is a prefecture-level reading of 'the north and east'; the pages give percentages and towns, no front lines.
